questions.q: Which format should be used to e-mail a document that must print identically everywhere?
questions.solution: **PDF** freezes fonts, layout and pictures on every device and printer.

questions.q: To **select the entire document** in one stroke, press —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+A** = select **A**ll — the whole document or every cells/rows in the active region.

questions.q: The national helpline number for reporting cyber fraud in India is —
questions.solution: **1930** — the national cyber-crime helpline (and cybercrime.gov.in online).

questions.q: Phishing messages delivered by SMS are called —
questions.solution: **Smishing** = SMS phishing — the bait travels by text message.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Occurrence: double c, double r, **-ence** ending. Occurance/Ocurrance take -ance; Occurence drops an r.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, "Alas! I am ruined."
options: He said with sorrow that he is ruined.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he is ruined.
He exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined.
He exclaimed with joy that he was ruined.
questions.solution: Alas → **exclaimed with sorrow**; am → was (backshift); I → he. B inverts the tone; C leaves the tense; D strands 'is'.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Rhythm has **no vowel except y**: Rh-y-th-m. Mnemonic: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move. Rhythem plants a fake e; Rythm drops the h.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: The true subject is **the number** (singular); *applicants* sits inside the 'of' phrase and cannot decide the verb. Part 2 must read **has doubled**. The other parts are grammatical.
questions.shortcut: Cover the 'of' phrase; the number is singular.

questions.q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.solution: The **liver** is the largest gland (and largest internal organ). It secretes bile, stores glycogen and detoxifies substances. The pituitary is the 'master gland', not the largest.

questions.q: **Ornithology** is the study of —
questions.solution: **Ornithology = birds** (Salim Ali, the birdman of India, was its greatest name here). Entomology is insects.

questions.q: To which deity are the **largest number of Rigvedic hymns** addressed?
questions.solution: **Indra** (~250 hymns; called *Purandara*, breaker of forts) leads, followed by **Agni** (~200). Varuna guards cosmic order (rita); Soma has Mandala IX.
questions.shortcut: Indra first, Agni second — keep the order.

questions.q: The **GST Council** was established under —
questions.solution: **Article 279A** (101st Amendment, 2016) creates the GST Council; 246A grants the taxing power and 269A handles IGST apportionment. 280 is the Finance Commission.

questions.q: A milkman mixes 1 litre of water with every 5 litres of milk and sells the mixture at the cost price of milk. His profit per cent is:
questions.solution: Profit $= \frac{\text{water}}{\text{milk}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{5} \times 100 = 20\%$.
questions.shortcut: Free water per honest litre = profit fraction ⇒ 20%.

questions.q: From 50 litres of a milk-water mixture in the ratio 4:1, 10 litres are removed and replaced with pure milk. The new ratio of milk to water is:
questions.solution: Draw removes 8 milk, 2 water → 32, 8; add 10 milk → $42:8 = 21:4$.
questions.shortcut: Here the milk column *grows* — the replacement is milk, not water.

questions.q: The base of a triangle is $15$ cm and its corresponding height is $8$ cm. Its area is:
questions.solution: $K = \frac12 \times 15 \times 8 = 60$ sq cm.

questions.q: 45 is what per cent of 360?
A clock seen in a mirror shows **9:10**. What will the **actual** time be 30 minutes later?
questions.solution: First convert the mirror reading: actual = 11:60 − 9:10 = 2:50. Then add 30 minutes: **3:20**. Adding first and converting afterwards gives 2:20, which is wrong because time passes on the real clock.
questions.shortcut: Convert to the actual time first, then add or subtract.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 118" width="154" height="118" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="113" x2="149" y2="113"/><line x1="149" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="5" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="41" y1="59" x2="77" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="113" x2="113" y2="59"/></svg>
questions.solution: The vertical line from the apex splits the triangle into 2 halves. Two lines from the base midpoint to the midpoints of the slanted sides cut each half into 2 → 4 smallest. The 2 halves themselves → 2. The whole triangle → 1. Total **7**.

questions.q: The figure shows the **mirror image** of a wall clock (the dot marks 12). What is the actual time?
questions.solution: The dot marks 12. Read the picture as it is: the hands show **7:50**. That is the mirror image, so the actual time = 11:60 − 7:50 = **4:10**. Check: 7:50 + 4:10 = 12:00.
questions.shortcut: Read the picture, then subtract from 11:60.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Farmers in a district report that a new type of pest has been damaging their standing crops.

**Courses of action:**
I. The farmers should be told to stop cultivation in the district.
II. Agricultural experts should be sent to identify the pest and advise the farmers on control measures.

Which of the courses of action logically follow(s)?
options: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
questions.solution: I is drastic and destroys the farmers' livelihood instead of tackling the pest — **does not follow**. II is a practical step that addresses the actual problem — **follows**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: Tackle the pest, not the farming.
